subject: history
title: Revolutions, Lenin and the Birth of the Soviet State
welcome_lead: From the February and October Revolutions to NEP and Lenin's death.
meta_desc: AQA A-Level adventure on the 1917 revolutions, Civil War, War Communism, NEP and Lenin's regime 1917-24.
final_note: You can trace how the Bolsheviks survived to entrench a one-party state.

concepts.def: Petrograd uprising in early March (Old Style February) that forced Nicholas II's abdication on 15 March 1917.
March-November 1917 coexistence of the Provisional Government and the Petrograd Soviet, weakening both.
Lenin's programme on return from exile (April 1917): 'Peace, Land, Bread' and 'All Power to the Soviets'.
Bolshevik seizure of Petrograd on 25 October (Old Style) / 7 November (New Style) 1917 by the Military Revolutionary Committee.
1918-21 emergency policies: grain requisitioning (prodrazvyorstka), nationalisation, labour conscription.
Lenin's tactical retreat permitting small-scale private trade and a tax in kind, introduced at the Tenth Party Congress.

walkthroughs.body_html: Wartime collapse (over 1.7 million Russian dead by 1917), the Tsarina's reliance on Rasputin (murdered December 1916) and bread riots in Petrograd (8-12 March) toppled Nicholas II. The Provisional Government under Lvov, then Kerensky, kept Russia in the war. Lenin's April Theses and the failed June Offensive shifted opinion. The Kornilov Affair (August) discredited Kerensky. On 25 October (OS) 1917, the Bolsheviks seized power.

The Treaty of Brest-Litovsk (3 March 1918) conceded vast territory to Germany. Trotsky built the Red Army (over 5 million strong by 1920). Whites under Kolchak, Denikin and Yudenich, plus Allied intervention, lacked unity. The Cheka (founded December 1917) conducted Red Terror. Famine in 1921-22 killed perhaps 5 million.

The Kronstadt Mutiny (March 1921) and peasant revolts forced the NEP. The same Tenth Congress banned factions. The USSR was constituted in December 1922. Lenin's Testament (December 1922-January 1923) criticised Stalin's rudeness. After strokes in 1922-23, Lenin died on 21 January 1924. A triumvirate of Zinoviev, Kamenev and Stalin sidelined Trotsky.
